compiled:
📰 General

Jason Bateman Reveals Reason for Limited Contact with Sister Justine Bateman •

Jason Bateman discussed his infrequent contact with his older sister, Justine Bateman, during an interview with Esquire. He explained that they don’t see each other “a ton,” citing differing lifestyles and priorities as the primary reason for the limited interaction. Bateman emphasized that they maintain a respectful and supportive relationship despite their infrequent meetings. The actor acknowledged Justine’s successful career as an actress and writer, highlighting their shared history and familial bond. He indicated that while they don’t see each other regularly, they remain connected.

🌍 World

IDF Seizes UNRWA Assets in Gaza Following “Yellow Line” Declaration •

Israeli police conducted a raid on the headquarters of UNRWA in Jerusalem, resulting in the seizure of IT equipment and other property. UNRWA Commissioner-General Philippe Lazzarini reported the incident, stating that the agency’s assets were taken. The action follows IDF Chief Aviv Kochavi’s declaration of a “yellow line” in Gaza, marking a new border demarcation. The agency has yet to comment on the full extent of the seized items or the implications of this action.

🦅 US

Powerful 7.6 Earthquake Off Japan’s Coast Triggers Tsunami Warnings •

A 7.6 magnitude earthquake occurred off the coast of northern Japan on Monday evening, prompting immediate tsunami warnings. The quake generated waves reaching up to 70 centimeters (27 inches) in coastal communities, particularly along the Pacific Ocean. Authorities issued alerts for potentially higher surges, urging residents in affected areas to evacuate to higher ground. The Japanese Meteorological Agency continues to monitor the situation and provide updates on wave forecasts.

💰 Business

Commerce Department Approves Limited Nvidia H200 Chip Exports to China •

The U.S. Department of Commerce is preparing to authorize the export of Nvidia’s H200 graphics processing units (GPUs) to China. This decision follows negotiations aimed at reaching a compromise regarding export controls. The H200 chips, approximately 18 months behind Nvidia’s current flagship offerings, will be permitted for specific applications, including artificial intelligence research and development. This represents a shift in policy, allowing access to advanced technology previously restricted.

💻 Technology

iOS 26.2 Release Delayed: New Beta Available for Testing •

Apple has released a second Release Candidate (RC) of iOS 26.2, intended for developers and public beta testers. This indicates a delay in the expected launch of the operating system, which was previously slated for this week. The RC provides a final opportunity for testing before the official release. Developers and testers can now access and report any remaining issues prior to the final version’s availability.

🎭 Entertainment

Trump’s Intervention Could Halt Netflix-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger •

President Donald Trump announced his intention to be involved in the review of the proposed merger between Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery. The Justice Department is currently scrutinizing the deal, citing concerns about market dominance and potential harm to streaming competition. Trump’s statement introduces a significant potential complication, as the White House could now directly influence the approval process. Legal experts suggest this intervention could delay or alter the outcome of the merger review.

🏅 Sports

Browns Coach Stefanski Announces Shedeur Sanders as Starting Quarterback •

Cleveland Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski has designated Shedeur Sanders as the team’s starting quarterback for the remaining four regular season games. This decision follows a period of evaluating backup quarterbacks, including Ty Simpson and Dante Moore. Stefanski stated the intention is for Sanders to demonstrate the Browns’ ability to effectively defend against top NFL draft quarterbacks. The move represents a significant opportunity for Sanders to solidify his position within the organization.

🔬 Science

New Fossil Discovery Reveals Ancient Human Relative Alongside Lucy’s Ancestors •

Scientists have identified the Burtele foot fossils, discovered in Ethiopia in 2009, as belonging to a previously unknown hominin species. Analysis of the bones, alongside more recent finds, suggests the species lived approximately 3.4 million years ago. This new species, tentatively named Burtele, coexisted with Australopithecus afarensis, the species to which Lucy, the famous “Ardi” fossil, belongs. The research provides crucial insights into the complex evolutionary relationships within the early hominin lineage.

🩺 Health

Norovirus Outbreak in Illinois Sparks Warnings Ahead of Holiday Season •

A highly contagious strain of norovirus, often referred to as “winter vomiting disease,” is currently spreading rapidly across Illinois. Health officials are reporting a significant increase in cases, primarily affecting schools and childcare facilities. The virus is characterized by symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and is spread through contaminated surfaces and person-to-person contact. Experts advise frequent handwashing and cleaning to prevent further transmission of the illness.
